algorithm.Title: Boil (Skin Abscess) - Male (Adult)
algorithm.ContentSet: IST Open-Source Guideline Content | Adult | Male
Definition: Boil/skin abscess assessment decomposed from NHS.UK's published when-to-get-help guidance.
FirstAid: Call Qatar 999 now. Do not squeeze, lance, cut, or apply caustic substances. Keep the patient still, do not allow self-driving, and follow the call-handler's instructions. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care.
algorithm.Author: IST Health Open-Source Guideline Content
algorithm.LastRevised: RESEARCH_REQUIRED - internal IST clinical adaptation date is not recorded

questions.Question: Is a widespread or flat localized rash the main concern, without a painful pus-filled lump or abscess?
questions.Information: The localized-rash family is not generated. Arrange in-person clinical assessment through the Qatar route approved by governance (GOVERNANCE_REQUIRED).

questions.Question: Is there confusion, collapse, abnormal breathing, pale/blue/mottled skin, rapidly spreading redness or swelling, severe pain out of proportion, black skin, or swelling around the eye, nose, jaw, or neck affecting vision, swallowing, or breathing?
questions.Information: Sepsis, necrotising infection, orbital spread, and airway involvement require immediate emergency assessment.

questions.Question: Without an emergency feature, is the boil on the face, near the eye, genitals, breast, spine, hand, or over a joint; is redness spreading or fever present; or is the patient an infant, pregnant, diabetic, immunocompromised, or otherwise seriously unwell?
questions.Information: NHS.UK boils guidance lists these as reasons for an urgent clinical review.

questions.Question: Has the boil lasted 2 weeks without improving, does the caller keep getting boils, or is there a cluster of boils (carbuncle)?
questions.Information: NHS.UK guidance recommends a routine primary-care review for a persistent boil, recurring boils, or a carbuncle.

questions.Question: Is this a single, recent boil with none of the features above?
questions.Information: NHS.UK guidance provides self-care steps (warm compresses) for an uncomplicated boil.

advice.Title: Emergency skin-infection precautions
Content: Call Qatar 999 now. Do not squeeze, lance, cut, or apply caustic substances. Keep the patient still, do not allow self-driving, and follow the call-handler's instructions. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care.
Call Back If: confusion, collapse, breathing change, rapidly spreading swelling, black skin, or severe pain.

advice.Title: Prompt in-person abscess review
Content: Use the Qatar governance-approved in-person service. Do not squeeze or pierce the lesion or use leftover antibiotics. Pregnancy, infant, diabetes, immune suppression, facial and genital lesions require clinician-led treatment.
Call Back If: spreading redness, fever, severe pain, or swelling near eye or airway.

advice.Title: Routine boil follow-up
Content: Arrange a routine primary-care review for a persistent, recurring, or clustered boil.
Call Back If: boil worsens; fever develops.

advice.Title: Care for a localized boil pending Qatar review
Content: Use a clean warm compress for short periods and keep the area clean and covered if it drains. Do not pick, squeeze, pierce, or apply caustic products, and do not share towels. Medicine choice and dose require age, weight, pregnancy or breastfeeding status, allergies, kidney or liver disease, ulcer or bleeding risk, other medicines, and Qatar formulary approval. This UAT branch remains non-telemedicine pending clinical governance.
Call Back If: boil lasts more than 2 weeks; signs of spreading infection or fever; pain or swelling rapidly worsens.
